ADR 0038: Cascade AppInstance removal through processes and schedules

description:
Operators manage systemd services and Docker containers owned directly by AppInstances through the existing `process:*` commands. Removing an AppInstance also removes its managed processes under [ADR 0038](<https://github.com/nckrtl/orbit/blob/main/docs/decisions/0038-cascade-appinstance-removal-through-processes-and-schedules.md>), and legacy process targets are unsupported under [ADR 0036](<https://github.com/nckrtl/orbit/blob/main/docs/decisions/0036-support-only-appinstances.md>).

## Scope

* In: AppInstance-only Process ownership, target resolution, API validation, typed SDK transport, CLI selectors, activity attribution, and the process Doctor family.
* In: development and production execution context, existing systemd and Docker lifecycle behavior, and AppInstance-removal integration.
* In: maintained process and AppInstance-removal documentation.
* Out: legacy Process record or runtime conversion, fleet preparation, Node-owned processes, new runtime backends, and Schedule implementation.
* Out: automatic process movement, source relocation, deployment orchestration, new Route policy, and harness changes.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Gateway, SDK, and CLI process operations accept only an AppInstance owner; `--instance` and the public `instance` target token resolve an AppInstance ID, while `--workspace` and Workspace targets are absent or rejected before mutation. Proof: `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Api/ProcessesTest.php`, `packages/php-sdk/tests/Unit/Requests/Processes/ProcessRequestsTest.php`, and `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Processes/ProcessCommandsTest.php`.
- [ ] A development target derives its Node, managed runtime user, recorded checkout, and environment-file path from the AppInstance; a production target derives its Node, dedicated runtime user, and recorded home from production placement, independent of Node role co-location or certificate mode. Proof: `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Domain/ProcessTargetResolverTest.php` and Incus action `appinstance-process-context`.
- [ ] Systemd retains its explicit working-directory option and defaults to the development checkout or the production `current` path, resolved afresh at each start; Docker retains its explicit image, command, environment, ports, volumes, restart policy, and container working-directory behavior. Caller input cannot select a different target Node or host execution user. Proof: `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Domain/ProcessActionsTest.php` and the systemd and Docker renderer suites.
- [ ] Development systemd processes receive the AppInstance certificate projection for its Route hostname through the existing Vite certificate environment variables and never refer to a legacy Instance or Workspace certificate path. Proof: `apps/gateway/tests/Unit/Infrastructure/Processes/SystemdProcessRendererTest.php` and Incus action `appinstance-process-tls`.
- [ ] Add, list, start, stop, restart, bounded logs, and remove complete for systemd and Docker processes on development and production AppInstances; runtime operations retain exact artifact-ownership checks, existing rollback behavior, and secret redaction. Proof: Incus action `appinstance-process-lifecycle` and `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Infrastructure/Processes/RemoteProcessRuntimeManagerTest.php`.
- [ ] Repeating an identical add resumes the same Process and preserves its desired state; a different specification with the same owner and name returns `process.name_taken` without modifying the existing process. Proof: `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Domain/ProcessActionsTest.php`.
- [ ] Unavailable or inactive targets refuse new or start operations before mutation; a provisioned release-layout target without `current` permits stopped installation but refuses starting a process until a release exists, while a removing or failed AppInstance still permits cleanup of its recorded owned processes when its Node is reachable. Proof: `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Domain/ProcessTargetResolverTest.php`.
- [ ] AppInstance source-preflight refusal leaves every owned process and its runtime unchanged; once removal is accepted, no new process can attach to any AppInstance in the fixed deletion set. Proof: `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Domain/AppInstanceProcessCascadeTest.php`.
- [ ] Normal and forced AppInstance removal stop and remove every owned running, stopped, failed, or removing process and its persistent runtime artifacts before reporting success; development source-removal and production home-retention rules remain intact. Proof: Incus action `appinstance-process-cascade`.
- [ ] A forced linked-worktree AppInstance cascade removes the processes of every AppInstance in the accepted deletion set and leaves sibling AppInstances outside that set, unrelated services, containers, and source untouched. Proof: Incus action `appinstance-process-cascade-isolation`.
- [ ] Cleanup failure keeps the AppInstance and unfinished Process cleanup resumable, reports no completed removal, and an identical retry completes only unfinished owned cleanup; an ownership conflict never authorizes artifact adoption or deletion. Proof: Incus action `appinstance-process-cascade-retry`.
- [ ] Process activities identify the owning AppInstance and its Node, and Doctor inspects the same target without mutation, including bounded reports for unavailable or incomplete removal state. Proof: `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Api/ProcessesTest.php`, `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Domain/ProcessDoctorProbeTest.php`, and Incus action `appinstance-process-doctor`.
- [ ] Maintained documentation states the AppInstance target, execution context, runtime options, cascade, failure, and operator-owned legacy transition boundaries, and generated context is current. Proof: `composer docs-lint`.
- [ ] Gateway, PHP SDK, CLI, and repository suites pass. Proof: `cd apps/gateway && composer check`, `cd packages/php-sdk && composer check`, `cd apps/cli && composer check`, and all five full no-TIA CI suites on the submitted candidate, plus focused affected Pest tests locally.
- [ ] A stopped Process completes installation without starting application code; an explicit start uses the then-selected production release, and an already running process is not restarted when the release pointer changes. Proof: Incus action `appinstance-process-release-context`.
- [ ] An operator changes an instance-specific process specification explicitly through remove and add; these operations address only instance-owned records, while an identical add preserves desired runtime state. Proof: `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Domain/ProcessActionsTest.php`.
title: Manage processes owned by AppInstances
